questions.question: A Pod has `restartPolicy: Never`, and one of its init containers fails during startup. Does Kubernetes retry that init container the way it normally would?
questions.gold_answer: No. Normally the kubelet repeatedly restarts a failing init container until it succeeds - but that behavior depends on the Pod's `restartPolicy`. With `restartPolicy: Never`, if an init container fails during startup, Kubernetes does not retry it at all and instead treats the whole Pod as failed.

questions.question: A Deployment has `.spec.revisionHistoryLimit` set to 2, and it has since been updated 5 times. You now want to roll back to the very first revision. Will that work?
questions.gold_answer: No. Rollback capability depends on the old ReplicaSets being retained, since each Deployment revision's configuration is stored in its corresponding ReplicaSet - once that ReplicaSet is deleted, you lose the ability to roll back to that revision. With `revisionHistoryLimit: 2`, only the 2 most recent old ReplicaSets are kept; after 5 updates, the ReplicaSet holding the first revision has almost certainly already been cleaned up, so you can no longer roll back to it.

questions.question: A StatefulSet has 5 replicas (ordinals 0-4) and `.spec.updateStrategy.rollingUpdate.partition` set to 3. If you update the Pod template, which Pods actually get updated?
questions.gold_answer: Only the Pods with an ordinal greater than or equal to the partition value - here, pod-3 and pod-4 (2 of the 5 Pods). Pods with an ordinal less than the partition (pod-0, pod-1, pod-2) are left on the old template and are not touched by the rollout, which is exactly what a partition is for: staging or canarying an update to only the highest-numbered Pods first.
